comparison: Both evaluations support the findings on biofilm formation and motility (C2, C3, C38-C40). OpenEval notes statistical significance and adequate sample sizes, while peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'overall solid' and 'effectively show[ing]' prophage effects on bacterial physiology. Both agree these phenotypic findings are well-supported.

Both address pdeB expression findings (C5, C41-C42, C44, C69), but with different evaluations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting the mechanistic connection remains correlative. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning why in vitro differences aren't observed and stating the manuscript 'primarily describes observations without providing insight into the molecular mechanisms.'

Both strongly support the colonization and spatial localization findings (C4, C47-C49, C63-C65). OpenEval notes statistical significance and appropriate replicates. Peer reviewers praise the 'striking microscopy' and describe this as a strength of the study, with the editor noting 'solid' evidence for niche occupation.

Both address differential retention findings (C45-C46, C67-C68), but with different emphasis. OpenEval supports the data while noting time-dependent effects and unclear mechanisms. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the biological interpretation, specifically questioning why increased retention ability didn't lead to greater cell retention at 24 hours.

Perfect agreement on VCBP-C expression findings (C7, C50, C72, C78). Both evaluations support the data showing prophage-mediated immune modulation. OpenEval notes limitations to one immune gene, while peer reviewers describe this as a key finding demonstrating 'mediation of host immune responses.'

Both support the findings on P5 expression reduction and VCBP-C effects (C8-C9, C53-C55, C76-C77). OpenEval notes the mechanism remains unclear. Peer reviewers accept this as novel and important, with Reviewer 2 highlighting the 'tripartite feedback loop' as interesting, though Reviewer 1 seeks more mechanistic detail.

Both support the negative result for multiple immune genes (C52). OpenEval notes this is important for understanding VCBP-C response specificity. Peer reviewers do not challenge this finding and accept the authors' caveat about host genetic diversity.

Both support the overarching tripartite model conclusions (C10, C59, C88). OpenEval notes the synthesis is reasonable though mechanistic details are incomplete. Peer reviewers strongly support this integrative conclusion, describing it as 'exciting research' with 'intriguing implications' and 'valuable' for linking prophage carriage to lifestyle regulation.

Both support the prophage deletion methodology and verification (C35-C37, C91). OpenEval details the molecular verification steps. Peer reviewers treat this as foundational and uncontroversial, accepting the mutant as properly constructed without questioning its validity.

Both support the reference gene validation methodology (C92). OpenEval notes this strengthens confidence in gene expression results and is often overlooked. Peer reviewers do not challenge this methodological detail, though Reviewer 1 questions the choice of qPCR over transcriptomics more broadly.

Both address C56 regarding SfPat classification. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the term 'distant relative' is vague and requires more rigorous support with no sequence identity or phylogenetic analysis provided. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on this bioinformatic classification.

OpenEval supports the contextualization claim (C60) comparing findings to prior work on prophages and biofilm formation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this comparative claim.

OpenEval supports extensive background and methodological claims (C1, C24-C29, C31, C89-C90, C93-C96) as well-supported and necessary context. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these background claims separately.

OpenEval supports numerous literature-cited background claims (C11-C23, C30, C32-C34, C43, C51, C61-C62, C66, C70, C73-C75, C79, C82, C84-C85, C87) as appropriately contextualizing the work. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these cited claims.

OpenEval rates speculative claims (C71, C80-C81, C83, C86) as UNCERTAIN, noting they extend beyond the data but are appropriately framed as hypotheses. Peer reviewers' R8 evaluation focuses on the supported tripartite model (C10, C59, C88) and includes some overlapping speculative claims (C71, C81) within their strong support for the overall conclusions.
